input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: Renewal terms meet our preferred position in full. § 8.2 provides automatic twelve-month (not multi-year) renewals that Customer alone may exit on only thirty days' written notice, with a Vendor reminder sixty days before renewal and an automatic extension of the opt-out deadline if the reminder is not sent — so the notice window is workable and cannot be missed through Vendor inaction. § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, requires ninety days' notice of any increase, and expressly excludes prepaid periods. § 8.1's three-year term is a fixed initial term, not an automatic multi-year renewal, and it does not lengthen the Order Form opt-out window. No redline needed.
